overview.purpose: A working overview for an agency owner reviewing sales outcomes, lead intake, attended appointments, and overdue work together. Use it to decide which underlying report deserves attention next.
overview.limitation: The sample combines a sales trend with top-customer ranking. Its operational counters remain separate facts; it does not label won deals as accounting revenue.

leads.purpose: Understand where recorded leads came from and how many have linked opportunities. This view helps a team inspect attribution coverage before making decisions from a source ranking.
leads.limitation: Source labels describe recorded CRM information. Unknown sources remain visible, and linked-opportunity outcomes do not establish advertising ROI.

pipeline.purpose: Review current open deals, sales progress, and follow-up exceptions in one worksheet. The chart arrangement is intended for a practical pipeline meeting rather than a decorative funnel.
pipeline.limitation: Stage bars are current-state snapshots. Historical stage conversion belongs in a separate history-based report; missing values and missing owners remain inspectable.

bookings.purpose: Compare appointment outcomes and attendance by calendar. Use the resolved attendance definitions to distinguish a recorded no-show from an appointment whose outcome has not been entered.
bookings.limitation: Show rate uses resolved attendance outcomes. Confirmed or unresolved appointments do not silently become attended appointments, and recurring occurrences retain their identities.

sales.purpose: Compare recorded won sales with goals you actually configured. Use the monthly actual-versus-target columns and current open-pipeline bars for a grounded performance review.
sales.limitation: Goals have a period, unit, and currency. A missing or incompatible goal is not a zero target; collected cash is measured by payment reports.

daily.purpose: Start the day with a queue of overdue tasks, upcoming appointments, and deals needing follow-up. The record table is the primary working surface.
daily.limitation: This is an as-of operational queue. Generic update timestamps are not task deadlines, and a completed flag is not proof of completion during a historical period.

team.purpose: Inspect sales and win-rate rankings by owner alongside owner trends. Four chart panels help explain the difference between who won value and who converted closed deals.
team.limitation: Win rate uses won divided by won plus lost in the qualifying cohort. Abandoned deals remain separate, and unknown ownership is not quietly dropped.

response.purpose: Inspect first verified human response, unanswered inquiries, and actor-classification coverage. This report helps teams see when a response metric is not sufficiently supported.
response.limitation: Bot and unknown outbound actors are not silently counted as human replies. Complete episode sequencing and validated actor classification are required for real results.

cash.purpose: Bring successful collections and current overdue invoices into the same operating view while keeping their meanings separate. Use the invoice register for collection follow-up.
cash.limitation: Gross live collections are not recognized revenue. Current overdue balances are snapshots, and a shared contact does not allocate a payment to a deal.

stages.purpose: Inspect observed conversion and completed time in stage to find supported bottlenecks. Compare median dwell with its P90 marker instead of relying on current stage counts.
stages.limitation: Only observed stage history can support this report. Pending observation windows, skipped stages, and repeat visits need explicit rules; current status alone is insufficient.

forecast.purpose: Review weighted opportunities and movement since a selected saved cutoff. This report makes configured probabilities and snapshot availability visible.
forecast.limitation: Weighted pipeline needs explicit probabilities and eligible close dates. Snapshot movement requires compatible saved coverage and is not a promise of forecast accuracy.

payments.purpose: Analyze successful payment collections, transaction counts, and payment types. Use this view when the decision concerns money collected rather than deals marked won.
payments.limitation: Test, failed, and other-currency transactions are separated from the displayed sum. Gross collections and current refunded totals must not be confused with accounting revenue.

receivables.purpose: Work an invoice-aging register of outstanding balances, from not-yet-due invoices to the oldest overdue bucket. This is a table-first report for collection work.
receivables.limitation: Balances describe the latest snapshot. Historical balance trends require actual snapshots; the sample does not invent a line chart from today’s balances.

invoice-items.purpose: Inspect invoice line amounts, quantities, and customer detail at invoice-line grain. Use this when header totals are too coarse for the question.
invoice-items.limitation: Do not repeat the invoice header total on every line when calculating a sum. Embedded lines are bundled with the parent invoice under the planned transfer-counting rules.

subscriptions.purpose: Review the current subscription mix, normalized recurring amounts, and billing-interval coverage. Use it to see which interval assumptions are supported.
subscriptions.limitation: A current cancelled status does not reveal the date of churn. Unknown billing intervals are excluded from normalization rather than guessed.

subscription-changes.purpose: Inspect recorded new, expansion, contraction, and churn events in a recurring-revenue waterfall. Each movement needs a real effective-dated event.
subscription-changes.limitation: The sample includes an invented event ledger. Live reporting requires accepted lifecycle history; current subscription flags cannot substitute for it.

orders.purpose: Review completed order value, order count, average order value, and pending orders. Keep the order header as the primary counting grain.
orders.limitation: Order value is not collected cash. Status and currency matter, and this report does not claim traffic conversion or gross margin without additional sources.

products.purpose: Inspect sold quantities and recorded sale-time product-line amounts. Missing catalog entries retain the labels recorded with the sale so historical lines remain readable.
products.limitation: Product-line amounts are distinct from order-header totals. No store visits, advertising return, or profit is inferred from the current product and order sources.

conversations.purpose: Review new conversations, assignment, and currently unread workload. Use the assignee breakdown to see how the sampled conversation volume is distributed.
conversations.limitation: Unread is a current flag, not an open/closed lifecycle. Conversation totals differ from the number of individual messages within those conversations.

messages.purpose: Inspect inbound and outbound message activity by date and channel. Keep verified human, automated, and unknown actors distinguishable.
messages.limitation: The preview uses message metadata. It does not establish live email-body export, call recordings, transcripts, or complete response-time sequencing.

capture.purpose: Review form and survey submissions, unique known contacts, and linked-opportunity coverage. Repeated responses remain separate submissions without becoming new contacts.
capture.limitation: Submission volume does not establish visitor-to-lead conversion. Form and survey identities stay distinct, and missing contact matches remain visible.

customer-payments.purpose: Inspect customer collections beside current balances after aggregating each financial source at its own grain. Use the customer table to explain contributing records.
customer-payments.limitation: A contact can have multiple payments and invoices. Joining first can multiply amounts; a customer match alone cannot allocate a payment to an opportunity.

businesses.purpose: Review business-linked contacts and the opportunities connected through those contacts. This account view highlights the difference between a known relationship and a familiar company name.
businesses.limitation: Business links use explicit source relationships. Company-name similarity is not treated as a validated association, and unlinked records remain disclosed.

activities.purpose: Inspect current task completion, overdue work, and dated note counts. This view helps a team understand workload without inventing a productivity score.
activities.limitation: A current completed flag is not a dated completion event. Notes are counted by their recorded dates; no note bodies or unsupported employee rankings are exposed.

custom-records.purpose: Explore a mapped Jobs example with status and customer-association coverage. The sample shows how a custom-schema report should make its required mapping explicit.
custom-records.limitation: The invented Jobs schema is not universal custom-object support. Production needs a selected schema, accepted source fields, and verified customer associations.
